beats: Hook: an analog computer can hold 0.37 on one wire, a digital one only 0 or 1 (reuse line_switch_dimmer: the toggle and the dimmer). Analog lost anyway. A qubit holds a continuum of values too; why is it not doomed the same way? Cast for all of QC01 (the six parts cut from her first lecture, Q25-01): the physicist (older, bald with a fluffy fringe, bushy moustache, goggles pushed up, lab coat) and the student (lanky, a tuft of hair, round glasses, striped long-sleeved T-shirt, messenger bag); both invented. No lecturer figure anywhere and never her likeness: her voice and her slides carry her part. For this part only: the 1950s engineer (side parting, thick-rimmed glasses, short sleeves, narrow tie, pocket protector).

Noise: qubit gates fail about once in 100 to 1,000 operations; classical logic almost never (her order of magnitude is 10^-15: source it or say "almost never"); classical machines correct errors too (reuse line_whisper_line: one slip every hundred hand-offs ruins a long chain).
The analog story: once seen as a more powerful replacement for digital (line_qc_analog_machine_room; clip 27:46-28:40).
Drift: a wire holding 0.4 creeps to 0.5 and nothing can tell (line_qc_analog_two_dials, the smooth dial).
Why digital wins: close to 1 means 1; every nudge rolls back to the bottom of its valley (line_qc_analog_two_valleys; the click-stop dial of line_qc_analog_two_dials says the same).

Her one-liner: computes like analog, corrects like digital (clip 31:03-31:32); her answer to the 0.5 question (35:42-36:42): a measurement always returns 0 or 1, so information is embedded the way bits embed it (line_qc_analog_coin_land, only as "every look returns one of two answers"; caveat in the narration: a spinning coin is an ordinary object with a definite face at every instant, a qubit is not, so never call the blur "both at once"). Do not use her cat line as a joke.

Threshold: below a noise level of roughly 1%-0.1% correction keeps up; at 20%, one error every five steps, it sinks (line_qc_analog_bail_boats; tape p10; values depend on the code and noise model, surface code ~1%).

Repetition-code intuition: send 000 for 0, vote at the other end (line_qc_analog_pigeon_vote; the three cards are blank and identical, code letters 0 0 1 on them). Copying a qubit is not allowed, so the quantum version needs a trick: QC08-01 and QC08-02.

The overhead is polynomial (polylog), the speed-up exponential: a small toll for a tunnel through the mountain (line_qc_analog_toll_tunnel; clip 33:54-34:22; threshold theorem: Aharonov and Ben-Or; Knill, Laflamme and Zurek; Kitaev; 1996-98).
Cover (line_qc_cover_01_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the 1950s engineer sweats at a drifting needle; the student clicks a two-position switch firmly into place.
